group.title: Things at home
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A piece of furniture with a flat top on legs.
wrong: I sleep in the table every night.

words.meaning: A seat for one person, with a back.
wrong: I drink coffee from a chair.

words.meaning: A piece of furniture that you sleep on.
examples: I go to {bed} at ten o’clock.
wrong: I cook dinner in my bed.

words.meaning: The thing you open to go in or out of a room.
wrong: I eat soup with a door.

words.meaning: A small piece of metal that opens a lock.
wrong: She opened the door with a banana.

words.meaning: A small container with a handle, for hot drinks.
examples: Would you like a {cup} of tea?
wrong: I wear a cup on my foot.

words.meaning: A flat round dish that you eat from.
wrong: I sleep on a plate.

words.meaning: A container made of glass that you drink from.
examples: Can I have a {glass} of water?
wrong: He wears a glass on his head.

words.meaning: A thing with a small bowl at the end, for eating soup.
wrong: I cut the meat with a spoon and a pen.

words.meaning: A thing with points at the end, for picking up food.
wrong: I drink water with a fork.

words.meaning: A thing with a sharp edge, for cutting.
wrong: I write a letter with a knife.

words.meaning: A container with flat sides, often with a lid.
wrong: A box is a kind of song.

words.meaning: A thing on a wall or table that shows the time.
wrong: I look at the clock to see the weather.

words.meaning: A thing that you use to talk to people far away.
wrong: I cook eggs in my phone.

words.meaning: A machine with a screen for watching programs.
wrong: I wash my clothes in the television.

words.meaning: A machine that you listen to for music and news.
examples: Dad listens to the {radio} in the car.
wrong: I watch films on the radio.

words.meaning: A machine that you use to write, play and go online.
examples: I do my homework on the {computer}.
wrong: I sleep on my computer every night.

words.meaning: A drawing, painting or photo.
examples: There is a {picture} of the sea on the wall.
wrong: I eat a picture for dinner.

words.meaning: The seat in a bathroom that you use to get rid of waste.
examples: The {toilet} is next to the shower.
wrong: We eat lunch in the toilet.

words.meaning: A thing that sprays water on you to wash your body.
wrong: I take a shower to get dry.

words.meaning: A thing you use with water to clean your body.
wrong: I put soap in my tea.

words.meaning: A large warm cover for a bed.
wrong: I put a blanket on my bed to feel cold.

words.meaning: A soft thing that you put your head on in bed.
wrong: I put my feet on the pillow and my head on the floor.

words.meaning: A thing that gives light, such as a lamp.
examples: Turn off the {light} when you leave.
wrong: I turn on the light to make the room dark.

words.meaning: The top cover of a building.
wrong: The roof is under the floor.

words.meaning: A part of a house with walls and a door.
wrong: A room is something you eat.

words.meaning: A long container that you fill with water and sit in to wash.
wrong: I take a bath in the oven.

words.meaning: A piece of glass that shows your face.
wrong: I look in the mirror to hear my voice.

words.meaning: A bell next to a door that visitors ring.
wrong: I ring the doorbell to turn on the oven.

words.meaning: A container for rubbish.
wrong: I keep my clean clothes in the bin.

words.meaning: Coins and paper notes that you use to buy things.
wrong: I buy shoes with water.

words.meaning: A thing for writing with ink.
wrong: I eat soup with a pen.

words.meaning: A thing for writing or drawing, made of wood.
wrong: A pencil is a kind of bird.

words.meaning: Thin material that you write on.
examples: Write it on a piece of {paper}.
wrong: I drink a glass of paper.

words.meaning: Pages with writing, fixed together inside a cover.
wrong: I listen to a book on the radio with my eyes closed.

words.meaning: A bicycle.
wrong: I wear my bike on my head.

words.meaning: A thing that children play with.
examples: The child has a new {toy} car.
wrong: A toy is a real car that adults drive to work.

words.meaning: The colored part of a plant.
wrong: I wear a flower on my feet as a shoe.

words.meaning: A tall plant with a wooden trunk and branches.
wrong: A tree is a small fish.

words.meaning: The clear liquid that falls as rain and that you drink.
wrong: I eat water with a fork.
